L1 to L7 come from one notebook, `Regression_Lecture1_Adv.ipynb`, L8 to L12 from a second, `Regression_Lecture2.ipynb`, L13 to L16 from `Regression_Lecture3.ipynb` (instrumental variables), L17 to L22 from `Regression_Lecture4.ipynb` (simultaneous equations) and L23 to L30 from `Regression_Lecture5.ipynb` (panel data): one lecture per major heading, with a mathematical appendix for each of the last three.

The course starts by **looking at the data**. [Econ 430 L1 Univariate Characterizations](note:econ-430-l1-univariate-characterizations) describes each variable on its own, with summary statistics, [Skewness and Kurtosis](note:skewness-and-kurtosis), histograms, [Kernel Density Estimation](note:kernel-density-estimation), the [Q-Q Plot](note:q-q-plot) and the [Cullen-Frey Graph](note:cullen-frey-graph); [Econ 430 L2 Bivariate Characterizations](note:econ-430-l2-bivariate-characterizations) looks at pairs, with scatterplots and the [Lowess Smoother](note:lowess-smoother) as a first check of linearity.

[Econ 430 L3 The Method of Least Squares](note:econ-430-l3-the-method-of-least-squares) is the core. It starts from the [Simple Linear Regression Model](note:simple-linear-regression-model) and the [SR Assumptions](note:sr-assumptions), derives the [OLS Estimator](note:ols-estimator), and shows that it is unbiased under linearity, [Strict Exogeneity](note:strict-exogeneity) and variation in $x$, and BLUE once [Homoskedasticity](note:homoskedasticity) and no autocorrelation are added ([Gauss-Markov Theorem](note:gauss-markov-theorem)). The [Sampling Distribution of OLS](note:sampling-distribution-of-ols) then supports inference: [Hypothesis Tests on Regression Coefficients](note:hypothesis-tests-on-regression-coefficients), the [Coefficient of Determination](note:coefficient-of-determination) and [Confidence vs Prediction Intervals](note:confidence-vs-prediction-intervals).

[Econ 430 L4 Cross-Validation and the Bootstrap](note:econ-430-l4-cross-validation-and-the-bootstrap) uses resampling to ask how well a model predicts new data ([Cross-Validation](note:cross-validation)) and how much its estimates would vary ([Bootstrapping OLS](note:bootstrapping-ols)). [Econ 430 L5 Estimating Nonlinear Relationships](note:econ-430-l5-estimating-nonlinear-relationships) fits curves by transforming variables ([Functional Forms and Elasticities](note:functional-forms-and-elasticities), [Box-Cox and Power Transformations](note:box-cox-and-power-transformations)). [Econ 430 L6 Indicator Variables and the OLS Workflow](note:econ-430-l6-indicator-variables-and-the-ols-workflow) adds categorical regressors ([Indicator Variables](note:indicator-variables)) and a seven-step workflow of fitting, testing and [Regression Diagnostics](note:regression-diagnostics). [Econ 430 L7 The Classical Linear Regression Model](note:econ-430-l7-the-classical-linear-regression-model) restates everything in matrix form: [OLS in Matrix Form](note:ols-in-matrix-form), the [Projection Matrix and Residual Maker](note:projection-matrix-and-residual-maker) and the [Conditional Mean vs Linear Projection](note:conditional-mean-vs-linear-projection). The matrix algebra it relies on is in [Math Prep](note:math-prep).

The second notebook moves to the [Multiple Regression Model](note:multiple-regression-model). [Econ 430 L8 Building Multiple Regression Models](note:econ-430-l8-building-multiple-regression-models) builds models on Big Andy's Burger Barn: linear combinations of coefficients, a quadratic with its [Marginal Effects](note:marginal-effects) and turning point, the [Delta Method](note:delta-method), factors ([Analysis of Variance](note:analysis-of-variance)), [Interaction Terms](note:interaction-terms) and the [F Test of Joint Hypotheses](note:f-test-of-joint-hypotheses), including the Chow test. [Econ 430 L9 Bootstrapping Regression Models](note:econ-430-l9-bootstrapping-regression-models) bootstraps a two-regressor model. [Econ 430 L10 Modeling Issues in Multiple Regression](note:econ-430-l10-modeling-issues-in-multiple-regression) covers specification: the [Component-Plus-Residual Plot](note:component-plus-residual-plot) and [Box-Tidwell Transformation](note:box-tidwell-transformation), [Omitted Variable Bias](note:omitted-variable-bias) and irrelevant variables, [Multicollinearity](note:multicollinearity), [Ramsey RESET](note:ramsey-reset), and choosing models with [Model Selection Criteria](note:model-selection-criteria) and [Variable Selection](note:variable-selection). [Econ 430 L11 Heteroskedasticity](note:econ-430-l11-heteroskedasticity) detects it ([Heteroskedasticity Tests](note:heteroskedasticity-tests)) and deals with it ([Heteroskedasticity-Consistent Standard Errors](note:heteroskedasticity-consistent-standard-errors), [Generalized Least Squares](note:generalized-least-squares)). [Econ 430 L12 Missing Data and the Regression Workflow](note:econ-430-l12-missing-data-and-the-regression-workflow) handles [Missing Data and Imputation](note:missing-data-and-imputation) and runs the whole workflow on a college-GPA example.

The third notebook turns to **endogeneity**. [Econ 430 L13 Linear Regression with Random Regressors](note:econ-430-l13-linear-regression-with-random-regressors) lets $x$ be random and shows that what matters is $\mathrm{Cov}(x, e)$: zero gives [consistency](note:consistency-and-probability-limits), nonzero gives an inconsistent OLS. [Econ 430 L14 When x and e Are Correlated](note:econ-430-l14-when-x-and-e-are-correlated) lists the three causes, [Classical Measurement Error](note:classical-measurement-error), simultaneity and [Omitted Variable Bias](note:omitted-variable-bias) (ability in a wage equation). [Econ 430 L15 Instrumental Variables Estimation](note:econ-430-l15-instrumental-variables-estimation) derives IV from the [Method of Moments](note:method-of-moments) and generalizes it to [Instrumental Variables and 2SLS](note:instrumental-variables-and-2sls); parents' schooling cuts the return to education from 10.75% to 6.14%. [Econ 430 L16 Specification Tests for Instrumental Variables](note:econ-430-l16-specification-tests-for-instrumental-variables) tests [Weak Instruments](note:weak-instruments), endogeneity ([Hausman Test](note:hausman-test)) and instrument validity ([Overidentifying Restrictions Test](note:overidentifying-restrictions-test)).

The fourth notebook covers **simultaneous equations**. [Econ 430 L17 Simultaneous Equations and Supply and Demand](note:econ-430-l17-simultaneous-equations-and-supply-and-demand) shows why price is correlated with both errors of a market ([Simultaneous Equations Model](note:simultaneous-equations-model)); [Econ 430 L18 Reduced-Form Equations](note:econ-430-l18-reduced-form-equations) solves for the reduced form and recovers the supply slope from it; [Econ 430 L19 The Failure of Least Squares and Identification](note:econ-430-l19-the-failure-of-least-squares-and-identification) signs the OLS bias and states the order and rank conditions ([Identification in Simultaneous Equations](note:identification-in-simultaneous-equations)); [Econ 430 L20 Two-Stage Least Squares for Simultaneous Equations](note:econ-430-l20-two-stage-least-squares-for-simultaneous-equations) estimates identified equations by 2SLS and 3SLS; [Econ 430 L21 Truffle Supply and Demand](note:econ-430-l21-truffle-supply-and-demand) and [Econ 430 L22 The Fulton Fish Market](note:econ-430-l22-the-fulton-fish-market) are worked examples.

The fifth notebook covers **panel data**. [Econ 430 L23 Panel Data and Microeconomic Panels](note:econ-430-l23-panel-data-and-microeconomic-panels) defines [Panel Data](note:panel-data); [Econ 430 L24 The Pooled Panel Model](note:econ-430-l24-the-pooled-panel-model) pools it with [Clustered Standard Errors](note:clustered-standard-errors); [Econ 430 L25 The Fixed Effects Model](note:econ-430-l25-the-fixed-effects-model) and [Econ 430 L26 The Random Effects Model](note:econ-430-l26-the-random-effects-model) model individual heterogeneity ([Fixed Effects Regression](note:fixed-effects-regression), [Random Effects Model](note:random-effects-model)); [Econ 430 L27 Comparing Fixed and Random Effects](note:econ-430-l27-comparing-fixed-and-random-effects) chooses between them with the Hausman test; [Econ 430 L28 Pooled, Fixed and Random Effects in Practice](note:econ-430-l28-pooled-fixed-and-random-effects-in-practice) runs everything on an airline cost panel; [Econ 430 L29 The Hausman-Taylor Estimator](note:econ-430-l29-the-hausman-taylor-estimator) recovers time-invariant effects ([Hausman-Taylor Estimator](note:hausman-taylor-estimator)); [Econ 430 L30 Sets of Regression Equations](note:econ-430-l30-sets-of-regression-equations) estimates one equation per firm with [Seemingly Unrelated Regressions](note:seemingly-unrelated-regressions).

The Fall 2025 midterm matches these weights: about half of it is interpretation of log, log-log and quadratic models, Box-Cox output, $t$ tests, $R^2$ and forecast intervals (L3 and L5), with one matrix derivation ($\mathbf{M}\mathbf{X} = \mathbf{0}$, L7), and short answers on bootstrapping, Q-Q plots and normality tests (L1, L4, L6). Its multiple-regression questions are L8 to L11: interpreting interactions and a linear combination of Andy's coefficients and finding a quadratic's turning point (L8), RESET, an irrelevant variable that inflates variances, AIC and BIC against $R^2$, and two Mallows' $C_p$ readings (L10), and Breusch-Pagan against White (L11).

sections.heading: If you only have one evening

blocks.md: Derive $\mathbf{b} = (\mathbf{X}'\mathbf{X})^{-1}\mathbf{X}'\mathbf{y}$ from scratch; prove $\mathbf{M}\mathbf{X} = \mathbf{0}$ and $\mathbf{M}\mathbf{M} = \mathbf{M}$; derive the four rows of the functional-form table by differentiating. Those three cover most of what the hard questions can touch.
